claim: The baseline defines TicketBunker as an intermediate agent layer between an agile tracker and git that receives ticket context, resolves branches, extracts git facts, enriches them through repository search, and returns a structured summary.

The baseline specifies a fixed six-stage bootstrap pipeline—branch resolution, baseline identification, diff extraction, merge history, work separation, and authorship—and classifies its outputs as atomic observations.
The baseline assigns the agent an enrichment phase that searches the base branch, compiles changed/new/old/candidate locations, and synthesizes who/what/where/why with labeled inference.
The baseline report contract defines Who, What, Where, Why, and State sections and identifies which sections combine observations with inference.

The baseline README says the project is in the design phase with no code yet, so the branch's ticketbunker package, harness integration, packaging, and tools have no baseline implementation counterpart.

The patch appears to turn the baseline design into a stdlib Python CLI that creates ticket bunkers, runs the ordered git-observation pipeline, composes and scaffolds agent context, records typed inferences, launches supported harnesses, gates branch reports, regenerates a master report, and synchronizes bunker state through git.

Because the baseline has no code, the ticket's implementation footprint is new work concentrated in ticketbunker/cli.py for orchestration; processors/stages.py and adapters/gitrun.py for git observations; types/, handlers/, builders/, and processors/reportlint.py for typed report flow; and adapters/harness.py plus harness/pi/tb.ts for agent-session integration.

Remaining automation described by the changed README likely belongs around ticketbunker/cli.py and ticketbunker/adapters/: git-hook triggers need a new repository-event boundary, while the root-surveyor session runner should connect the existing survey command and context fragments to a harness invocation.

The branch appears intended to make ticket reconstruction auditable by keeping deterministic git facts outside agent control, labeling repository findings and interpretations, and accepting reports only through typed and linted intake.

The branch appears to satisfy the ticket's core local end-to-end workflow, but it is not merged and the changed README still identifies git-hook triggers and the root-surveyor session runner as unbuilt, with the real-model pi path awaiting credentials.
No additional implementation owner or reviewer is named in the baseline ticket-related material beyond the ticket-configured person.
The baseline identifies the motivating gap as the manual reconstruction of who changed what, on which branch and baseline, and why when agile-ticket context drifts from git history.
